market_summary: Tuesday's US session ended flat: S&P 500 -0.02% to 7,805, Nasdaq -0.15% to 27,204, Dow -0.35% (-180 pts) to 51,670, as the chip index fell a fifth straight day (Applied Materials -6.5%, Roundhill memory ETF -3.5% on CXMT worries) while Meta rose 2.5%; the 10-year Treasury eased 3bp to 5.21%, WTI rose 0.8% to $94.45 and Brent slipped 0.6% to about $106, and NY Fed's Williams said one more hike this year is still appropriate but he does not expect another in 2027. Banks beat but sold: all four closed lower (Citi about -5.5%, KBW bank index -1.1%) even though Goldman earned $17.01 a share vs $13.09 expected and Citi $2.85 vs $2.65, while JPMorgan missed ($5.75 adjusted vs about $5.92) and Wells Fargo's revenue and net interest income fell short. Wednesday in Asia the chip rebound faded: KOSPI was up about 1.6% at midday but closed -0.44% at 6,008.81 on foreign selling (KOSDAQ -1.57%), the Nikkei gave up a 0.6% midday gain to end about flat near 67,744, the Hang Seng was about -0.2% near 24,280 in the afternoon, Shanghai about +0.1% at midday and the ASX 200 about -0.7%. China's September exports jumped 36.3% y/y (25.5% expected) and imports 31% (24.5% expected) for a $133.5B surplus, while PPI rose 5.0% y/y (4.5% expected, the fastest since June 2022, on oil and metals) and CPI 0.9% (1.0% expected). ASML reported Q3 sales of EUR 11.66B and a 57.5% gross margin, lifted its 2026 sales guide to EUR 44-45B (from 43-45B), guided Q4 to EUR 14.2-15.2B and said its 2027-28 supply plans will not fully meet demand. In Asian trade Nasdaq 100 futures were +0.3% and S&P 500 futures +0.1%, Brent +1.2% to about $106.86 and WTI +0.8% to $94.96; gold futures were $4,190 and bitcoin about $83,100 late Tuesday ET. Next: Bank of America 21:45 AEDT and Morgan Stanley 22:30 AEDT tonight; US CPI 23:30 AEDT Wed (core seen +0.2% m/m); US open 00:30 AEDT Thu; Beige Book 05:00 AEDT Thu; Anthropic investor session Wed US (Thu AEDT); AU jobs 11:30 AEDT Thu; TSMC 17:00 AEDT Thu; PPI, retail sales and claims 23:30 AEDT Thu; Warsh 14:30 AEDT Fri; options expiry Fri US; FOMC blackout from Sat Oct 17; China Q3 GDP 13:00 AEDT Mon Oct 19; Netflix 07:01 AEDT Wed Oct 21; Meta and TI 07:30, IBM and Lam 08:00, Tesla 08:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22.

AMZN.reason: Down 0.4% Tuesday, a third small decline. No follow-up found on the WSJ-reported Decart talks (about $7 billion, unsigned). Alexa tablets go on sale today, Wed Oct 14; Q3 about Fri Oct 30 07:00 AEDT. Hold.

AXOS.reason: Down 0.6% Tuesday on no company news. Bank results were mixed for the sector: JPMorgan missed on EPS for the first time in about three years and cut buybacks, Wells Fargo and Citi beat, and the KBW bank index fell 1.1%. BAC and MS report before tonight's US open (about 22:00-22:45 AEDT), then CPI 23:30 AEDT; Axos fiscal Q1 Fri Oct 30 08:00 AEDT. Hold.

BABA.reason: US ADR flat (+0.1%) Tuesday. China's September exports rose about 36% against 25.5% expected and factory prices rose 5%, the fastest since June 2022, while consumer prices missed at 0.9%. No company news; China Q3 GDP Mon Oct 19 13:00 AEDT, results Nov 24. Hold.

ENPH.reason: Up 1.7% Tuesday, recovering part of Monday's 4.0% drop, with no company or policy news. The 10-year Treasury yield sat at 5.21%; US CPI tonight 23:30 AEDT is the rate test. Q3 call Wed Oct 28 07:30 AEDT. Watch.

FIGR.reason: Fell 4.3% Tuesday with no company news found, giving back Friday's 3.4% gain as mortgage and lending names stayed weak (Rocket hit a 52-week low). The bank index fell 1.1% after JPMorgan's EPS miss. CPI tonight 23:30 AEDT; Q3 date still unannounced. Hold.

GOOGL.reason: Up 0.3% Tuesday, a third straight small gain while the Nasdaq slipped 0.15%. No company news. ASML said AI demand lifted its Q3 profit to a record €5.0 billion and raised guidance, which supports the capex cycle Google Cloud sells into. Q3 results late October. Add stays.

LDI.reason: Fell 4.8% Tuesday, erasing most of Monday's 3.6% bounce, as Rocket hit a 52-week low after JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley cut targets. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year eased 0.02 points to 7.46%, a two-week low but still near three-year highs. Still below the NYSE one-dollar threshold; CPI tonight 23:30 AEDT. Trim.

META.reason: Rose 2.6% Tuesday after 3.4% Monday, as Meta launched Muse Wonder, its first frontier model, priced at $4/$20 per million input/output tokens through its API; Meta's benchmark claims are not independently verified. No New Mexico penalty ruling yet (expected by late October). Q3 results Wed Oct 21 after the US close, call 07:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22. Hold.

MRVL.reason: Up 1.1% Tuesday after Monday's 3.4% fall, with no company news. ASML raised its 2026 guide and said 2027-28 tool supply will not fully meet AI demand. TSMC's Q3 call Thu 17:00 AEDT is the next AI-demand read. Hold.

MU.reason: Fell 3.6% Tuesday, a third straight loss (about 7% over two sessions), on China's CXMT DRAM push and a 99% vote by workers at Micron's Taoyuan, Taiwan plant to authorise a strike over a demand for 15% of quarterly operating profit; no strike date is set. Korea did not bounce: KOSPI faded from a midday gain to close -0.4% Wednesday, SK hynix -1.7%. DDR5 spot still topped $60 for the first time. Hold, but watch the strike.

NFLX.reason: Down 0.2% Tuesday. Netflix has still not confirmed the roughly 5% job cuts (about 800 roles) Puck reported and declined to comment. Q3 results Wed Oct 21 07:00 AEDT, guided to $12.86 billion revenue (+12%). Hold into the print.

NVDA.reason: Up 1.0% Tuesday, recovering most of Monday's 1.3% loss. No update on the FT-reported Reflection AI talks. ASML's Q3 (record €5.0 billion profit, guidance raised on AI demand) supports the supply chain; TSMC's Q3 call Thu 17:00 AEDT, then GTC Berlin Oct 20-22. Hold.

RKT.reason: Down 0.4% Tuesday to a new 52-week low, a fourth straight decline, after JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley cut their targets; the stock is down 44% this year. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year eased to 7.46%, still near three-year highs. CPI tonight 23:30 AEDT; Q3 around Oct 29. Watch.

TSM.reason: ADR up 0.2% Tuesday; Taipei shares were flat Wednesday as the Taiex rose 0.6%. ASML, a key TSMC supplier, reported Q3 sales of €11.7 billion and raised guidance on AI demand. TSMC already reported Q3 revenue of about $46.7 billion; results and guidance Thu Oct 15 17:00 AEDT. Add stays.

STRIPE.reason: No new round, tender or secondary mark found; the last company tender was February at $159 billion, so the mark multiple stays 2.27. No company news found for Oct 13-14. Hold.

OPENAI.reason: No close reported for the roughly $30 billion round at about $1.4 trillion pre-money (talks with MGX-led UAE funds and BlackRock per Bloomberg Oct 5), so the mark multiple stays 5.43. Meta's Muse Wonder launch adds a priced frontier-model competitor. Anthropic's investor session Thu AEDT is the next private-AI reference. Hold.

headlines: ASML beat on profit, raised its 2026 guide to EUR 44-45B and said 2027-28 tool supply will fall short of AI demand.
Micron fell 3.6%, a third straight loss, as Taiwan plant workers voted 99% to authorise a strike; Korea's bounce faded Wednesday.
Banks beat but sold off as JPMorgan missed; Rocket hit a 52-week low, loanDepot fell 4.8% and Figure 4.3%.
Meta rose 2.6% after launching Muse Wonder, its first frontier model, on top of Monday's 3.4% gain.
China's September exports rose 36% against 25.5% expected; factory prices rose 5.0%, the fastest since 2022.
Next: US CPI 23:30 AEDT tonight (core seen +0.2%), Anthropic investor session Thu AEDT, TSMC results Thu 17:00 AEDT.
